title: introduce 'callset' API: resumable multi-tool orchestration + deterministic parallel injection
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add new 'callset' orchestration API to support deterministic, resumable multi-tool executions. Backwards compatible mapping layer provided for OpenAI functions format. Migration notes included.
description:
Motivation: Developers need a succinct, ergonomic way to express sets of tool/function calls that can run in parallel or sequentially, be retried idempotently, and have results deterministically injected back into the model context. Existing surfaces either forced single-tool sequential flows or ad-hoc orchestration at the application layer. This PR introduces the "callset" first-class API and runtime plumbing to make multi-tool workflows reliable, observable, and compatible with OpenAI-style function calls.

Summary of changes: Introduce API surface 'callset' which accepts an ordered list of tool descriptors and a run_mode (parallel|sequential|ordered-concurrent). Each callset receives a callset_id and an optional resume_token; runtime guarantees idempotent replay when retries happen and deterministic injection ordering based on the provided ordering rules. Add an OpenAI compatibility mapper that translates incoming function-calls arrays into callsets and maps callset results back to OpenAI function return shapes. Provide SDK helpers (Python/TS) and Console UI support for debugging/resuming callsets.

Key implementation details: single-shot controller + call worker pool: controller serializes callset metadata, selects affinity for tools (GPU vs CPU), and enqueues tasks; worker pool executes tool invocations with an execution token, produces a per-tool result envelope that includes attempt_count and run_metadata; result injector is deterministic — when run_mode=ordered-concurrent we preserve original index order while allowing out-of-order completion. Resume semantics: resume_token encodes last-applied index and worker-checkpoint; replay is idempotent using per-tool idempotency_keys derived from callset_id + tool_index + user-provided key. Retry semantics: Built-in hedging policy when a tool is slow: schedule a speculative retry to a warm worker in a different zone. Backpressure: callset-level concurrency cap and per-tool rate limits.

OpenAI compatibility: api/openai_compat/mapper.py implements to_callset() and from_callset() that accept legacy function-calls and produce callsets. When clients use the OpenAI functions shape, we attach a shim header 'X-Redwood-Callset-ID' and set run_mode to 'ordered-concurrent' by default to mirror common function-call expectations.

Migration and compatibility: existing single-tool calls are untouched. The OpenAI mapper is opt-in by default via header or via SDK flag; we do provide a server-side toggle in Console to enable automatic mapping for customers who want transparent compatibility. SDKs include helpers so customers can migrate incrementally.

Files changed (high-level): service/handlers/callset_controller.py - new controller and API handler; runtime/worker_pool.py - added callset scheduling and hedging; api/openai_compat/mapper.py - compatibility layer for functions->callset; sdk/python/redwood/callset.py - ergonomic helper and examples; sdk/ts/src/callset.ts - TypeScript helper + types; console/src/components/CallsetDebugger.tsx - new UI to inspect/resume callsets; docs/api/callset.md - spec and migration guide; tests/test_callset_end2end.py - integration coverage.

Commits: ["3f2a7b2 - introduce callset controller and basic handler","8b11cde - add worker_pool hedging and per-tool idempotency keys","d9a4f10 - openai_compat mapper + tests","a04ccb7 - python/ts SDK helpers and examples","f5e9d88 - console callset debugger UI and telemetry hooks","b21c3f1 - docs and migration guide, add release notes"]

Testing and CI: Unit tests added across controller, mapper and SDKs. Integration tests cover ordered-concurrent semantics, resume flows, and idempotency. CI history: initial run (unit-tests) failed due to a race in test harness (fixed in 8b11cde), integration tests initially flaked in one matrix cell and passed after rerun. Perf check: microbenchmarks show 1.8% CPU overhead in controller path at small sizes but a 12-18% latency improvement for multi-tool callsets due to reduced round-trips and improved worker affinity; no customer-facing regression observed in smoke fleet.

Review summary and conversation (condensed):
- Jonah Kim: "Can we guarantee that speculative retries won't produce duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent tools?"
- Aisha (author): "We require callers to provide an idempotency_key per tool or rely on callset-derived idempotency_key. For tools that cannot be made idempotent, there's a 'no_retry' flag at tool descriptor level. Added doc note + validation."
- Sofia Alvarez: "I'm worried about observable signal in Console for partial-completed callsets."
- Aisha: "Added CallsetDebugger with per-tool status, attempt history, and a resume button that replays with the same callset_id. Also emit a 'callset.progress' event to telemetry."
- Marcus Reed: "OpenAI compatibility shim might surprise users if mapping semantics differ."
- Aisha: "Default mapping mirrors our earlier heuristic; added opt-out and explicit server toggle. Documented edge cases in docs/api/callset.md."

Approvals: Jonah Kim - approved after idempotency doc update; Sofia Alvarez - approved after UI additions; Marcus Reed - approved after explicit opt-out added.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'callset_enabled' tenant flag. Gradual rollout: 1% of traffic for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> 100% for opt-in tenants. Monitor: callset.failure_rate, callset.latency.p50/p95, tool.retry_rate, hedged_retries, and errors surfaced in Console. Auto-rollback triggers defined (failure_rate > 2% sustained for 15m).

Follow-ups: (1) implement quota accounting per callset ticket (ENG-3451) to prevent large fanout from bypassing quotas; (2) add richer structured output schema validation for call results (DES-122); (3) add a small-batch optimized kernel path to further reduce controller overhead.

Merge: squash merge to main. Merge commit: 0a9f3b7.

Notes for maintainers: watch the worker_pool logs for hedged-invocation patterns in first 48 hours of rollout; telemetry tags include callset_id and tenant_id. The docs include sample migration snippets for both Python and TS SDKs.
